# Localzet Server

> Localzet Server is an event-driven PHP server runtime for applications that need long-lived connections, multiple network protocols, and worker process management.

## Project

- Official documentation: https://server.localzet.com/
- Source repository: https://github.com/localzet/Server
- Current stable release: Localzet Server 7.2.3. Its incremental HTTP parser bounds memory use and multipart requests are limited to 1,024 parts by default. The TLS `onConnect` callback runs only after a successful handshake; plain TCP behavior is unchanged. HTTP and WebSocket codecs close a TLS connection when ALPN selects anything other than `http/1.1`; HTTP/2 is not implemented. Integration coverage includes trusted, missing, and untrusted client certificates. Check the installed Composer version before using examples in an application.
- License: AGPL-3.0-or-later.
- Runtime requirement: PHP 8.1 or newer with ext-json and ext-ctype. Unix multiprocess supervision requires pcntl and posix.

## Capabilities

- HTTP/1.x over PHP streams, including TLS configuration, streaming file responses, and Server-Sent Events.
- WebSocket, raw TCP, UDP, and an interface for application-defined protocols and message framing.
- Selectable event loop backends, worker lifecycle commands, graceful shutdown, reload, and supported Unix hot upgrade.
- HTTP/1.x reverse proxy and raw TCP proxy components with upstream pooling.
- Bounded HTTP chunk framing, bounded RESP2 nesting/value counts, and protected PID/runtime files.
- Optional Redis and MongoDB session handlers.

## Best fit

Consider Localzet Server when a PHP application needs long-lived connections, custom TCP message framing, WebSocket communication, or direct control over worker lifecycle and event loop backends. Evaluate the application on its own workload and infrastructure before choosing it for a latency or capacity target.

## Important limits

- The runtime does not implement HTTP/2 or HTTP/3.
- It does not provide application authentication, authorization, rate limiting, service discovery, or API management.
- Performance depends on the application and deployment environment; the project does not publish universal throughput or connection-capacity guarantees.
- Examples in the current handbook describe the current source tree. Verify package version and API compatibility before upgrading an existing application.

## Related Localzet projects

- [Cluster](https://server.localzet.com/projects/cluster): release 1.1.0, gateway/worker cluster for Server 7; Federation listeners and clients use the Server 7 protocol contract without a wire-format change. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/Cluster/releases/tag/v1.1.0).
- [Cron](https://server.localzet.com/projects/cron): release 2.0.1, timer-based scheduling for Server 7; removing a job cancels its pending one-shot timers. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/Cron/releases/tag/v2.0.1).
- [Console](https://server.localzet.com/projects/console): release 2.3.0, PHP CLI library with Symfony Console by default, an opt-in Laravel command bridge, Unicode/ANSI helpers and bounded terminal dashboards. Requires PHP 8.4.1+. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/Console/releases/tag/v2.3.0).
- [HTTP Client](https://server.localzet.com/projects/httpclient): release 3.0.2, asynchronous HTTP requests and connection pooling for Server 7; verifies TLS peers by default and strips sensitive headers on cross-origin redirects. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/HttpClient/releases/tag/v3.0.2).
- [MQTT](https://server.localzet.com/projects/mqtt): release 1.0.3, MQTT 3.1.1 and MQTT 5 client with TCP/TLS, QoS 0/1/2, and legacy Server protocol aliases; debug logs redact credentials, topics, properties, and payloads. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/MQTT/releases/tag/v1.0.3).
- [PSR-7](https://server.localzet.com/projects/psr7): release 4.0.0, HTTP messages, streams and URI helpers for Server 7. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/PSR-7/releases/tag/v4.0.0).
- [Proxy](https://server.localzet.com/projects/proxy): release 1.0.3, HTTP forward proxy for Server 7 with Basic authentication and an exact literal-IP/port allowlist. Complete headers are limited to 16 KiB and five seconds; proxy-only credentials are removed before forwarding, and the default client limit is 256 connections per worker. Use TLS and egress ACLs. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/Proxy/releases/tag/v1.0.3).
- [SOCKS5](https://server.localzet.com/projects/socks5): release 1.0.1, TCP CONNECT proxy; default configuration binds to loopback. Per-worker attempt tracking is bounded to 10,000 source IPs. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/SOCKS5/releases/tag/v1.0.1).
- [Socket.IO](https://server.localzet.com/projects/socketio): release 2.0.3, in-memory adapter by default; its optional cross-process adapter is compatible with Tunnel 4.x. Room subscriptions remain active while any local socket remains in the room. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/SocketIO/releases/tag/v2.0.3).
- [Storage](https://server.localzet.com/projects/storage): release 2.0.1, PHP 8.2+ in-memory store for Server 7; rejects objects and recursive arrays by default, limits frames to 64 MiB, and validates up to 100,000 array values and 128 levels of nesting before decoding. Install from the Git VCS source because it is not on Packagist. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/Storage/releases/tag/v2.0.1).
- [Tunnel](https://server.localzet.com/projects/tunnel): release 4.0.2, inter-process messaging with process-wide limits of 10,000 pending queue messages and 32 MiB of queued request bytes; objects and recursive arrays are rejected by default. Debug logs redact message payloads and raw exceptions. Over-limit enqueue is rejected without acknowledgement, and transport authentication is not built in. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/Tunnel/releases/tag/v4.0.2).
- [Noter](https://server.localzet.com/projects/noter): release 0.1.14, PHP 8.4.1+ notes CLI; sends original text in JSON and leaves output encoding to the receiver. Its self-contained PHAR bundles Localzet HTTP 3.0.1, Console 2.2.2, PSR-7 4.0.0, and Server 7.2.3. [Release and PHAR](https://github.com/localzet/Noter/releases/tag/v0.1.14).
- [Triangle Media](https://server.localzet.com/projects/media): latest published tag `v1.1.0` requires Triangle Engine `^8.1`; the prepared major `2.0.0` targets Engine 9 and Server 7 but is not yet published. The guides cover installation, compatibility, configuration, uploads, ImageMagick filters, security, and tests in English and Russian. [Source](https://github.com/Triangle-org/Media), [migration status](https://github.com/Triangle-org/Media/pulls).

## Triangle Engine family

The current stable tags are Localzet Server 7.2.3, Triangle Engine 9.0.0, Router 2.0.7, Middleware 2.0.3, Console 2.0.0, Database 2.0.0, Session 2.0.0, Events 2.0.1, and View 2.1.0. Engine 9 requires Server `^7.1`, so the Server 7.2.3 tag satisfies its declared Composer constraint. Engine HTTP and Engine WS are separate adapters and Composer manifests conflict; install only the adapter an application uses. Check Composer's resolved versions in the application's lock file.

- [Triangle Engine](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine): release 9.0.0 for PHP 8.1+ and Localzet Server `^7.1`. [Requirements](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine/requirements), [installation](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine/install), [architecture](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine/architecture), [compatibility with Engine 8](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine/compatibility), and [test limits](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine/testing). [Release notes](https://github.com/Triangle-org/Engine/releases/tag/v9.0.0).
- [Triangle Engine HTTP](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http): release 3.0.0 for Engine 9, Router 2, Middleware 2, Server 7.1+, PHP 8.1+, and ext-curl. Its install guide contains a runnable HTTP listener and curl check. CORS is disabled by default. [Compatibility](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http/compatibility), [security](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http/security), and [tests](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http/testing). [Release notes](https://github.com/Triangle-org/Engine-HTTP/releases/tag/v3.0.0).
- [Triangle Engine WS](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws): release 2.0.0 for Engine 9, Router 2, Middleware 2, and Server 7.1+. Its install guide contains a runnable WebSocket listener and echo route. Connection groups are process-local; cross-process delivery requires a separate broker or IPC component. [Compatibility](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws/compatibility), [security](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws/security), and [tests](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws/testing). [Release notes](https://github.com/Triangle-org/Engine-WS/releases/tag/v2.0.0).
- [Engine HTTP installation](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http/install), [request handling](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http/requests), [security](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http/security), and [test limits](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http/testing).
- [Engine WS installation](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws/install), [handshake and messages](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws/messages), [security](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws/security), and [test limits](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws/testing).
- [Compatibility and migration](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine/compatibility): Engine 8.1.11 targets Server 4; Engine 9.0.0 targets Server 7.1. The comparison documents changed Composer constraints, global helpers, and Fiber context behavior.
- [Triangle Console](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-console): release 2.0.0, a Triangle Engine 9 application command layer; PHP 8.4.1+, Localzet Console 2.2+, Symfony Console/Process 8.1+. It is separate from Localzet Console. [English guide](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-console/en).
- [Triangle Database](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-database): release 2.0.0, Illuminate database/Eloquent integration for Engine 9; PHP 8.2+, Illuminate 12, Server 7. [English guide](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-database/en).
- [Triangle Session](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-session): release 2.0.0, Engine 9 session handlers; PHP 8.1+, Server 7.1+. PHP objects from serialized storage are not instantiated by default. [English guide](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-session/en).
- [Triangle Events](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-events): release 2.0.1, synchronous in-process dispatch for exact and prefix event names; it is not a durable or cross-worker queue. The patch fixes logger initialization when a listener throws and tests that exceptions are returned by `Events::emit()`. [English guide](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-events/en), [release notes](https://github.com/Triangle-org/Events/releases/tag/v2.0.1).
- [Triangle View](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-view): release 2.1.0, PHP `.phtml` rendering by default with optional template adapters; supports Engine 8 and 9. Raw templates do not auto-escape output. [English guide](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-view/en).
- [Triangle Router](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-router): release 2.0.7, HTTP route matching and dispatch for Engine 8 and 9. Route matching does not authorize requests or replace application HTTP semantics. [English guide](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-router/en).
- [Triangle Middleware](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-middleware): release 2.0.3, middleware contracts and configuration for Engine 8 and 9; the package does not itself run an HTTP server. [English guide](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-middleware/en).
- [Triangle Cron](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-cron): published release 1.0.3 targets Engine 8.1; Engine 9 source is not tagged or published. Do not request the preview `^2.0` constraint from Packagist. [English guide](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-cron/en).
- [Triangle OAuth](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-oauth): published release 3.0.9 requires PHP 8.2+ and Localzet HTTP 2; the current checkout adds an Engine dependency beyond the published tag. [English guide](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-oauth/en).
- [Triangle Web](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-web): release 8.0.1 project template for Engine 8.1, HTTP adapter 2, PHP 8.2+. Its published template is not an Engine 9 starter. [English guide](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-web/en).
- [Triangle WS](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-ws): published release 1.0.4 targets Engine 8.1 and Engine WS 2; current checkout uses Engine WS 1.1. Default runtime is one worker and local sends do not cross processes. [English guide](https://server.localzet.com/projects/triangle-ws/en).
